name: Race condition (single-packet)
description:
The application enforces a single-use limit as check-then-set with a window between the check and the record: the same request sent one at a time succeeded exactly once, but a synchronized group of requests — every member's last byte released together — succeeded more than once with one token. This is the single-packet attack: the group arrives within one check-then-set window, so every member passes the check before any member's record lands. The same primitive over-redeems coupons and vouchers, double-spends balances, and defeats one-per-actor limits on votes, claims and invitations.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no race-condition row; PortSwigger ships the single-packet attack as the Turbo Intruder extension, whose issues carry the generic extension-generated type.
remediation: Enforce single-use limits atomically: a database unique constraint with an insert that fails on conflict, a conditional update whose WHERE clause includes the not-yet-redeemed predicate, or a lock held across the check and the record. Never check and then set in separate steps. Where the limit is financial, reconcile per-token success counts against the ledger.
